label: lem:initial-regularity
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
At $q=0$, Jensen's inequality gives
 egin{equation*}
 \psi_{
u,h}(0)+\int h\,\mathrm d
u
 =-\log\int e^h\,\mathrm d
u+\int h\,\mathrm d
u\leqslant0.
\end{equation*}
Equality holds for $h=0$, so $\varphi^
u(0)=0$. By Lemma~ef{lem:regularity}, each function $q\mapsto\psi_{
u,h}(q)+\int h\,\mathrm d
u$ is $1$-Lipschitz in $L^1$ and $\mathcal{Q}_2^*$-increasing on $\mathcal{Q}_2$. Taking the supremum in~\eqref{eq:initial-definition} preserves these properties and gives $\varphi^
u(q)\leqslant|q|_{L^1}$. 
Since $q\in\mathcal{Q}_2$ implies $q\in\mathcal{Q}_2^*$, monotonicity gives $\varphi^
u(q)\geqslant\varphi^
u(0)=0$ there. 
Approximation by bounded paths extends this lower bound to $\mathcal{Q}_1$.

label: lem:Parisi-diffusion
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
In column-stacked coordinates,~\eqref{eq:Parisi-PDE} has covariance path $I_N\otimes q$, coefficient $\alpha(s)=s$, and terminal measure $\Lambda_{\mathbf{g}}$. Existence and regularity follow from~\cite[Proposition 4.7(1), (3), and (4)]{chen2024simultaneous}. Its cascade representation~\cite[Lemma 4.5, (4.10)]{chen2024simultaneous} gives~\eqref{e.F_N=-1/NEPhi} after averaging over $(\mathbf{g},\mathbf{z}_0)$.
                                                                                                                                                                              
Differentiating in $\mathbf{x}_{\cdot,i}$ gives a linear backward equation whose terminal gradient lies in the unit ball. The maximum principle gives the column bound. The bounded Hessian makes the drift of~\eqref{eq:diffusion} globally Lipschitz, giving a unique strong solution; see also~\cite[Proposition 3.2]{chen2023parisi}.
The finite terminal sum and the same regularity estimates justify the parameter differentiations below: derivatives in $(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{g})$ and in bounded terminal perturbations are bounded, while the $t$ derivative has at most linear growth in $\mathbf{g}$ locally on $t>0$.

label: lem:step-residual
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:step-residual}
Proposition~\ref{prop:residual} also holds at $q=L_Ka+\varepsilon\ell$, where $a\in\mathcal{Q}^K$ and $\ell:[0,1]\to S^D_+$ is given by $\ell(s):=sI_D$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $a\in\mathcal{Q}^K$ and let $\widehat q_a:\mathbb{R}\to S^D_+$ be the extension of $L_Ka$ that is constant on $(-\infty,0)$ and $[1,\infty)$. Choose a nonnegative $\kappa\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb{R})$ with $\int_\mathbb{R}\kappa=1$. For $\eta>0$, define $\kappa_\eta(r):=\eta^{-1}\kappa(r/\eta)$ and $q_\eta^0:=\kappa_\eta*\widehat q_a$. Since $\widehat q_a$ is positive semidefinite and increasing, the same holds for $q_\eta^0$. In addition, $q_\eta^0$ is smooth, and the 
    standard mollifying argument
    gives $\lim_{\eta\downarrow0}|q_\eta^0-L_Ka|_{L^1}=0$.
Consequently, $q_\eta:=q_\eta^0+\varepsilon\ell$ satisfies $ 
\overset{\mbox{\large\bfseries .}}{q}_\eta(s)\succeq\varepsilon I_D$ for every $s\in[0,1]$ and $\lim_{\eta\downarrow0}|q_\eta-(L_Ka+\varepsilon\ell)|_{L^1}=0$.

We apply Proposition~\ref{prop:residual} to $q_\eta$ and let $\eta\downarrow0$, with $N,t,K,a,\varepsilon$ fixed. Equation~\eqref{eq:gradient-continuity} gives convergence of the path derivatives in $L^1$. The time derivative is continuous as well: the bounded replica representation in~\eqref{eq:replica-derivatives}, differentiated along a Gaussian interpolation, gives
\begin{equation*}
 |\partial_t\overline F_N^\nu(t,q)-\partial_t\overline F_N^\nu(t,q')|
 \leqslant C NM_0|q-q'|_{L^1}.
\end{equation*}
Let $q_*:=L_Ka+\varepsilon\ell$. For fixed $N$, both derivatives therefore converge as $\eta\downarrow0$. Their path components have $L^\infty$ norm at most one by Lemma~\ref{lem:regularity}, so
\begin{equation*}
 \left|\int_0^1\xi(\partial_q\overline F_N^\nu(t,q_\eta,s))\,\mathrm d s
 -\int_0^1\xi(\partial_q\overline F_N^\nu(t,q_*,s))\,\mathrm d s\right|
 \leqslant M_1|\partial_q\overline F_N^\nu(t,q_\eta)-\partial_q\overline F_N^\nu(t,q_*)|_{L^1}\longrightarrow0.
\end{equation*}
The residual bound at $q_\eta$ is independent of $\eta$ and passes to $q_*$.
